Issue #300: Fix intermittent public navigation cache test failure without weakening CI (T15)
Issue URL: https://github.com/jboone1989/EventGraph/issues/300
## Task
Fix the real non-deterministic CI web test failure observed in [PR #299 Check attempt 1](https://github.com/jboone1989/EventGraph/actions/runs/41472728497): `apps/web/tests/cache.test.ts:53-64` occasionally fails at `assert.ok(answers.every((body) => body === answers[0]))` when four public `_.data` loader-route variants are requested concurrently, while the unchanged test passed on an exact-head single-job retry. This is a **CI integrity** task: diagnose actual differing bytes/fields before changing the assertion; do not simply weaken it or hide errors.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Reproduce or capture enough diagnostic evidence to explain which loader data fields or stream encoding vary, with original and updated test behavior.
- [ ] Make the test deterministic while preserving a falsifiable assertion that all routes return the same *complete public navigation content*, and keep the separate category-filter inequality and cache headers/expiry checks.
- [ ] Add a negative test or equivalent focused proof that a genuine missing/different navigation payload still fails. Do not use retries, sleeps, indiscriminate normalization, ignored fields, or conditional skipping merely to get CI green.
- [ ] Run relevant focused tests and full required Check/Docker/E2E; document any unrelated failure. Limit changes to the existing cache test and the actual source of nondeterminism, with no production/server deployment.

acceptance_criteria: `docs/admin-ui-reuse.md` explicitly starts with a **product contract** for feature Specs (user outcome and entry, CRUD data/meaning, complete user journey, list/search/page choices, states/error feedback, responsive/long data, preservation/non-goals, Given/When/Then acceptance). It gives clear examples of a deficient “add CRUD” Spec and an adequate compact one. Business-significant decisions, such as hard vs. soft deletion or impact on associated data, require an explicit authorized basis, not invented defaults.

The same guide then maps the current `AdminPage`, `DataTable`, `Pager`, `Select`, `Button`, `ReasonDialog`, etc. to actual `develop` file paths, documents limitations and says when to use an existing feature/installed dependency or investigate a maintained external component. It prohibits gratuitous reimplementation, but does not force pagination where unnecessary.

The existing `spec-review` prompt in `.github/workflows/check.yml` tests *material* product contract completeness and user-visible acceptance first, before worrying about technical decisions. It flags unclear operation semantics, omitted main states or untestable criteria with a file/line finding; it does not demand a rigid form for every small fix.

`AGENTS.md`, `.agents/CONSTRAINTS.md` and the current `.github/workflows/eventgraph-worker.md` link the canonical guide. The Worker reads the pinned Spec, checks missing/contradictory product rules, researches reuse, implements only accepted behavior, and records a compact **acceptance → implementation → test/browsing result** matrix and reuse choice in its original implementation PR.

The existing central implementation reviewer checks the actual PR diff against both the approved Spec and applicable product defaults; demonstrated bad CRUD UX, misleading “working” controls, long IDs crushing columns, omitted meaningful error feedback, or needless duplicate components are actionable blockers. Existing review model/schema, check names and automatic merge contract remain intact.

Focused tests verify that the two existing reviewer entrypoints and Worker are connected to these rules, and sample scenarios demonstrate that an incomplete CRUD Spec is rejected while a concise but sufficient one is not mechanically blocked. The tests cannot claim to guarantee LLM correctness or actual UI rendering.
Existing Check/Docker/E2E and independent review must pass; do not claim deployed features or fixed admin pages from this instruction-only task. No extra PRs for the same Work Item.
